newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea denies calling off Cargill barter deal.
newsitem.headline: North Korea denies calling off Cargill barter deal.

text.p: North Korea has denied calling off a zinc-for-wheat barter deal with Cargill Inc and accused the U.S. grain giant of spreading "groundless rumours".

"The contract is still under discussion because of some different opinions which occured in the course of its implementation," North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) quoted a North Korean trade official as saying in a report which ran late on Wednesday.

"Nevertheless, Cargill Inc is setting abroad groundless rumours that the contract was unilaterally abrogated by the DPRK (North Korea) because it is receiving sufficient food from the international community," the chief secretary of the Korean committee for the promotion of international trade told KCNA.
The report was monitored in Tokyo.

Earlier this month, Cargill said famine-hit North Korea pulled out of the barter deal, worth $4 million on each side, without any explanation. The deal, finalised in early April, called for the U.S. grains giant to swap 20,000 tonnes of wheat for 4,000 tonnes of North Korean zinc.
"By hurling mud at the DPRK, the company revealed its true intention to hurt the DPRK," the North Korean official was quoted as saying.
"We will surmount the present temporary food shortage by our own efforts at any cost," he said.
